No  ORDER

This misc. appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is preferred by the claimant/appellants challenging the impugned award dated 27.06.2017 passed by the MACT, Indore in claim case No.37/2015 whereby the Claims Tribunal partly allowed the claim case and granted compensation to the tune of Rs.16,82,000/- alongwith interest @ 6% p.a.
2.

Brief facts of the case are that on 31.01.2014 at around 5:30 pm deceased Vardichand aged about 43 years met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.2/driver of the offending vehicle as result of which the deceased sustained grievous injuries and died during the treatment.

Thereafter, the legal representatives of the deceased filed an application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 seeking compensation to the tune of Rs.60,00,000/- alongwith interest on account of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3563 2 MA-2787-2017 death of Vardichand.

3. The learned Tribunal found that the accident has been caused by the respondent no.2 due to his rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle which was owned by respondent No.1 and insured with respondent No.3.
Thus, the learned Tribunal has awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.16,82,000/- against the claim of Rs. 60,00,000/- before the Tribunal.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the Tribunal has wrongly assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.12,000/- per month which is on the lower side.
He further submitted that Tribunal has also not awarded single penny towards future prospects.

Thus, the counsel for the Smt. Uma@ Umrao vs Dharmendra Thru. Smt. Deepa on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167365574/
1 appellant submits that compensation awarded deserves to be enhanced.

sentences.text: 5 . Refuting the submissions made by learned counsel for the appellants, learned counsel for the respondent No.3 submitted that the findings arrived at by the learned Tribunal are just and proper and does not require any interference by this Court under this appeal.
6. It is not in dispute that respondent no.2 was responsible for causing the accident and on the fateful day, the offending vehicle was insured with respondent no.3.
The only question for determination in this appeal is as to whether the amount awarded by the Claim's Tribunal requires any modification.

7. Having heard the rival submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and going through the material and evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that the learned Tribunal has assessed the income of deceased on lower side.

Admittedly, on the date of accident i.e.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3563 3 MA-2787-2017 31.01.2014, the deceased was aged about 43 years and as per the Madhya Pradesh State Legal Service Authority guidelines, the income of unskilled labour was Rs.15,500/- per month whereas the learned Tribunal has wrongly assessed the income of deceased as Rs.12,000/- per month only.

entities.text: Madhya Pradesh State Legal Service Authority
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 8. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, this Court found that the income of the deceased would be considered as Rs.15,500/- in place of Rs.12,000/- per month.

The yearly income of the deceased would come to Rs.1,86,000/-.
9.

Therefore, after applying the law laid-down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 4 ACJ 270 and Sarla Verma &
Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Others reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, the claimant is entitled to get the compensation as under:-
Loss of dependency : 24,41,250/-
(Annual Income 1,86,000 + 25% future prospect - 1/4 personal expenses x multiplier of 14) Loss of consortium : 2,00,000/-
 Loss of Estate : 15,000/-

10.

Therefore, in addition to the award which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal, the appellant is entitled to get the enhanced compensation amount to the tune of Rs.9,89,250/- (Rs.26,71,250/- - Rs.16,82,000/-) on various heads.
The enhanced amount shall carry same interest as has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.

Rest of the conditions, as imposed by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:3563 4 MA-2787-2017 learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed to the extent indicated herein above subject to following conditions:-
i.
The respondent-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 30 days from the date of this order, failing which the execution can be taken out against him.
ii. The claimants are directed to pay the requisite Court Fee, if required in the present case.
Office is also directed to verify whether any Court Fees is payable for the enhanced compensation amount.
iii. On such deposit, the claimants are permitted to withdraw the amount with accrued interest and costs, by filing a proper application before the Tribunal.
iv. The impugned award of the learned Tribunal stands modified to the aforesaid extent and in terms and directions as above.
v. The record be sent back to the learned Tribunal within three weeks from this day.
(HIMANSHU JOSHI) JUDGE akanksha Smt. Uma@ Umrao vs Dharmendra Thru.
